title: Quick access assumes system tray in bottom-right corner

fix_assessment.rationale: The current Quick Access show and prime paths both call PositionWindowBottomRight, and the helper deliberately places the window at the bottom-right of the work area on the cursor monitor. It does not use the notification-area icon or taskbar edge. A taskbar-aware placement change is applicable, although the exact activation anchor and fallback behavior need maintainer reproduction across supported taskbar positions.

proposed_fixes.title: Place Quick Access relative to the PowerToys tray icon
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Quick Access uses a fixed bottom-right work-area placement rather than the taskbar or tray-icon position. This directly explains the reported placement when the taskbar is on the left or top.
plan: Resolve the PowerToys notification-area/taskbar anchor when Quick Access is summoned and pass it to the shared flyout placement path used by both ShowWindow and PrimeWindow.
Place the flyout beside the anchor according to the taskbar edge, clamp it to the selected monitor's work area, and preserve a safe bottom-right fallback when the anchor cannot be resolved.
Add placement tests for bottom, top, left, and right taskbars, including non-primary monitors and DPI scaling.
verification: On Windows 10 22H2 and a supported Windows 11 build, open Quick Access from the PowerToys tray icon with the taskbar at the bottom, top, left, and right; verify the popup opens adjacent to the icon.
Repeat on a secondary monitor and at non-default display scaling; verify the popup remains within the correct work area and does not overlap the taskbar.

confidence.rationale: The hard-coded bottom-right behavior is confirmed in both Quick Access placement paths and directly matches the report. The tray activation anchor and edge-selection implementation have not yet been exercised on movable taskbars, so their integration details still need a focused reproduction.

issue_context.summary: Quick Access opens at the bottom-right of the monitor instead of beside the PowerToys notification-area icon when the taskbar is moved.
known_information: The reporter uses PowerToys 0.97.2 on Windows 10 22H2 and says the taskbar is unlocked and moved to the left or top edge.
The expected behavior is to open next to the system-tray icon, either automatically or through a position setting.
A second commenter confirmed the same behavior with a top-positioned taskbar.
A November 5 commenter notes that a recent Windows 11 update adds taskbar-position settings; this is not a new reproduction result.
A November 5 maintainer reply confirms a related report was closed as a duplicate of #45712, which remains the canonical tracking issue; the reply does not establish that a fix has shipped.
Current source still uses fixed bottom-right placement for both Quick Access show and prime paths.
inferences: The current fixed placement logic is the direct reason the popup does not follow a non-bottom taskbar.
The exact tray-icon activation coordinates may not be available to Quick Access today; a maintainer should verify the supported anchor source and fallback before implementation.
issue_context.analysis: MainWindow.ShowWindow and PrimeWindow both call FlyoutWindowHelper.PositionWindowBottomRight. That helper selects the monitor under the cursor and positions the window at the work area bottom-right, without taskbar-edge or tray-icon input. The latest maintainer reply confirms a related report is a duplicate of this canonical issue, but no merged or released fix is established and current source still has the fixed placement. Keep the taskbar-aware proposal on this tracker and verify the supported anchor/fallback behavior before detailed design.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue report, both comments, labels, and current live update time; there is no assignee or maintainer ownership.
Inspected QuickAccess.UI/QuickAccessXAML/MainWindow.xaml.cs: both ShowWindow and PrimeWindow call PositionWindowBottomRight.
Inspected Common.UI.Controls/Window/FlyoutWindowHelper.cs: the helper selects the cursor monitor and computes placement from the bottom-right of its work area.
Read related issue #51600; it is closed but describes a similar Quick Access and Power Display taskbar-placement request, not a verified fix.
Re-read the November 5 follow-up: a maintainer says the related report was closed as a duplicate of #45712; checked current upstream/fork PR search and found no matching PR.

judgment.rationale: The issue still has a concrete placement defect: current Quick Access paths use fixed bottom-right positioning. A new maintainer reply confirms a related report was closed as a duplicate of #45712 and says this issue tracks the work; that establishes #45712 as the canonical thread but does not establish that a fix has shipped. The current source still uses the fixed placement, so retain the proposal while avoiding a competing duplicate.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep #45712 as the canonical tracker, verify any proposed implementation against the current fixed-placement code, and reproduce taskbar-edge behavior before approving a detailed design.
evidence: The report and confirmation describe Quick Access appearing bottom-right when the taskbar is on the left or top.
Both Quick Access placement paths call PositionWindowBottomRight, which ignores the taskbar and tray-icon location.
The related closed #51600 is not evidence that the current Quick Access implementation was changed.
A November 5 maintainer reply confirms that a related report was closed as a duplicate of #45712 and that this issue tracks the work; it does not report a merged or released fix.

actions.label: Verify Quick Access placement on moved taskbars

reproduce.title: Check Quick Access placement against taskbar position
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys; include Windows 10 22H2 and a supported Windows 11 build when available.
prerequisites: Unlock the Windows taskbar and make the PowerToys notification-area icon visible.
steps: Move the taskbar to the left edge and click the PowerToys notification-area icon.
Repeat with the taskbar at the top and right edges.
Repeat from a secondary monitor if available and record the monitor and display scaling.
reproduce.expected_result: Quick Access opens next to the PowerToys tray icon on the same display and remains within the work area without covering the taskbar.
